name: Percentage-biased differential current relay
summary: Differential relay form whose operating threshold rises in proportion to the through current, set as a relative value.
description: This relay form represents differential protection where the operate quantity is the difference between currents entering and leaving a zone, and the threshold is a percentage of the through current. The bias keeps the relay stable when CT errors grow during heavy external faults or transformer tap changes.

On a drawing the relay box is fed from CT sets at each boundary of the protected zone. The symbol does not show the slope settings, the harmonic restraint used for transformer inrush, or the vector-group and ratio compensation, all of which must be taken from the relay settings record.
readingNotes: Locate every CT set that bounds the protected zone.
Check CT polarity so through current cancels in the relay.
distinction: A biased differential relay raises its threshold with through current; a plain differential current relay uses a fixed threshold.
